newsitem.title: JAPAN: Gore says will raise human rights issues in China.
newsitem.headline: Gore says will raise human rights issues in China.

text.p: U.S. Vice President Al Gore said on Monday he would raise human rights issues with Chinese leaders on his visit to Beijing but had no plans for specific meetings with human rights activists.

But in a brief meeting with reporters shortly before his departure for Beijing after a 24-hour stay in Tokyo, Gore said he could not rule out talks with activists at U.S. embassy functions while he was in China.

Asked what U.S. concerns he would raise in Beijing, Gore replied: "I will, of course, discuss human rights in my meetings with the leadership of China, nor will it be a surprise to them to hear these matters raised."
But he added: "I have no specific meeting of that kind (planned with human rights activists)."

Gore's trip to China, part of an Asian tour that also includes South Korea, is aimed at healing ties between Washington and Beijing and paving the way for an exchange of visits by U.S. President Bill Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin over the next year.
